question: Should OpenClaw accept `currentTokenCount` plus the token-budget helper exports as a stable public ContextEngine/plugin SDK contract now, or fold that token signal into the broader assemble metadata design?
rationale: The patch adds public plugin API and SDK exports that third-party context engines may compile against, while related assemble metadata work remains open and could absorb or reshape this contract.

options.title: Accept Narrow Contract After Fixes
options.body: Approve `currentTokenCount` as a focused backward-compatible API after the two patch blockers and real behavior proof gap are resolved.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Metadata
options.body: Pause this PR and ship token-budget metadata with the broader provenance/internal-event assemble metadata design instead.

options.title: Keep Helpers Private For Now
options.body: Remove the SDK helper exports and defer public helper exposure until the context-engine API shape is settled.

recommendation.title: Accept Narrow Contract After Fixes
recommendation.body: Approve `currentTokenCount` as a focused backward-compatible API after the two patch blockers and real behavior proof gap are resolved.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned and have the strongest recent merged history on the context-engine API and token-budget paths.
